name: Jets
author: Sixth Front
description: AVIATION BATTLES ONLY (pick AVIATION on the main menu). Fighter jets for both sides. Vanguard flies the F-16C Viper, F/A-18E Super Hornet, A-10C Warthog, F-15E Strike Eagle and the stealthy F-35A Lightning II and F-22A Raptor; Onyx flies the MiG-29 Fulcrum, Su-27 Flanker, Su-25 Frogfoot, Su-35S, Su-34 Fullback and the stealthy Su-57 Felon. Stealth jets are harder to lock on to, radar missiles (AIM-120, R-77) reach twice as far as heat seekers and shrug off most flares, and guided bombs (JDAM, KAB) glide onto a target near where they would land. Pick a jet on the deploy screen and you start in the air. Steer with the mouse (or drag on a phone), or switch FLIGHT CONTROLS to JOYSTICK in the settings to fly with the stick or W/S/A/D (with an INVERT PITCH option). Throttle with afterburner, 1/2/3 weapons: cannon, heat-seeking missiles with lock-on, and bombs, rockets or guided missiles. Space drops flares, E ejects with a parachute. Bots fly them too: dogfights, strafing runs and bombing. Flight is real physics (thrust, lift that stalls past the critical angle, drag, gravity, and the airframe swinging its nose into the airflow) under a fly-by-wire limiter, so the tightest turns come near corner speed and a vertical climb runs out of speed. No buttons for manoeuvres: in the Su-27, Su-35S, Su-57, MiG-29 and F-22A a sharp, hard pull from level flight (flick the aim far up, or snap the stick back) overrides the limiter and flies Pugachev's Cobra, the nose rearing past vertical while the jet slides on and brakes hard (hold it in a thrust-vectoring jet for the Kulbit); in any jet, climb straight up with the throttle back until the speed is gone and it slides back on its tail until the nose swings down through, the Kvochur Bell. Shoot a wing and it breaks off and the jet spins in; a shot-off fin or tailplane leaves it hard to fly. Every jet dispenses flares its own way (Flankers fan them out of the tail, US fighters drop them from the belly, the A-10 and Su-25 ripple long strings). The chase camera frames each jet the same way, the whole aircraft in the lower half of the screen; afterburners burn as glowing plumes with shock diamonds, cannon tracers fly out as white-hot streaks with a muzzle flash and spray or dust where the rounds land, contrails stream off the wingtips, a jet skimming the sea throws up spray, and the picture blurs at the edges at speed. The HUD has a compass radar, the pilots' names and a top view of your aircraft showing which parts are hit. On a phone the buttons change when you fly: the weapons by name (GUN, MISSILE, BOMBS... with what's left), FLARES, CAMERA, ZOOM and SPOT, EJECT up by the pause button, a throttle slider on the left, a big round fire button, and you steer by dragging anywhere.
